## Caption (verbatim)

```
Michael is mentioned by name only four times in Scripture.
Four times. That's it. And every single mention involves war.
The first time — Daniel 10:13 — he battles a demonic prince for twenty-one straight days to deliver God's message to the prophet Daniel. The angel sent to Daniel couldn't break through on his own. He needed Michael. "Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me."
The second time — Daniel 12:1 — he is called "the great prince who protects your people" and is described as the one who will arise during the worst tribulation the world has ever seen. When the darkest hour comes, Michael stands up.
The third time — Jude 1:9 — he confronts the devil himself over the body of Moses. And here's what's remarkable: even as the most powerful angel in heaven, Michael doesn't boast. He doesn't flex his authority. He says five words: "The Lord rebuke you." His power comes from God alone.
The fourth time — Revelation 12:7-9 — he leads heaven's entire army against the dragon. "And there was war in heaven. Michael and his angels fought against the dragon… and the great dragon was hurled down — that ancient serpent called the devil, or Satan."
He won.
That serpent was cast to earth. And Michael's mission didn't end there.
His name — Mikha'el in Hebrew — means "Who is like God?" It's not a question. It's a war cry. A direct challenge to Satan's pride, to Lucifer's original sin of believing he could become like God.
Michael's entire existence is the answer: No one.
The Church named him protector of the faithful for a reason. He's been fighting since before time. He's fighting now. And when you call on him — when you pray "St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle" — you're calling on the angel who already proved he could defeat the enemy of your soul.
He's not retired. He's not symbolic. He's real, he's biblical, and he's still on the battlefield.
"Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back. But he was not strong enough, and they lost their place in heaven."
— Revelation 12:7-8
```
